clue.text: Hit back at old city friend-of course!

indicators.note: back tells us the word for hit is to be read from right to left

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat or thrash them
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone retaliates against a friend from an ancient city, exclaiming that of course they would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAN into NAT, which is followed by UR and ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of agreement, saying something is only to be expected.

clue.text: Sailor who wants to be a priest

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman longs to give up the sea and take holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French title for a cleric, especially an abbot or secular priest.

clue.text: Let us in to cook something in the kitchen

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so the letters of the phrase are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be admitted so they can prepare a meal with kitchen gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cook' rearranges the letters of LET US IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement such as a spoon or whisk, a typical item found in a kitchen.

clue.text: Stuffy song was shortened

parts.note: an air is a tune or simple song
less is read as an old participle sense, made less, cut down in size

explanation.surface: A tune in a stuffy room was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter treats 'was shortened' loosely as LESS, the sense 'made smaller'.
explanation.definitionFit: A room without fresh ventilation feels close and stale, lacking any breeze.

clue.text: Wasted a fortune around the first of September

indicators.note: around has the word for fortune wrapped round the letter from September

parts.note: lot means one's fate or fortune

indicators.note: the first of picks out just the opening letter of September

explanation.surface: A gambler blew a fortune in early autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts S, from 'the first of September', inside LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Time or effort that is lost has been squandered to no purpose.

clue.text: Men who fleece the absentminded

explanation.surface: Swindlers prey on forgetful people.
explanation.walkthrough: Wool-gatherers literally collect fleece; woolgathering also means daydreaming, so the absent-minded are woolgatherers too.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherers of wool collect fleeces from sheep, and to woolgather is to let one's mind wander idly.

clue.text: Altruism gets corrupted by money in a group of chemists

indicators.note: corrupted text is garbled, so these letters are scrambled together

parts.note: L stands for pound, the British unit of money (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A selfless instinct is spoilt by cash among some laboratory scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges ALTRUISM, GETS and L together.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallurgists are scientists who study the chemistry and properties of metals.

clue.text: Cheated when swimming the channel both ways

definitions.text: when swimming the channel both ways

explanation.surface: A long-distance swimmer is accused of foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: To cross the Channel there and back is literally to cross it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone is to deceive them, and a swimmer who makes the crossing twice has literally crossed again.

clue.text: Might be found on the road in front of a car because of bad back-a desperate situation

definitions.text: Might be found on the road in front of a car

indicators.note: back tells us the word for bad is turned round

parts.note: mal is French for bad, familiar from words like malpractice
a plight is a dangerous or difficult predicament

explanation.surface: A motorist with a bad back finds the road ahead full of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses MAL to give LAM, followed by PLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlights cast illumination onto the road ahead of a moving vehicle at night.

clue.text: Coppelia's got herself mixed up with church government

indicators.note: the ballet heroine getting confused means her letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: The ballet heroine Coppélia becomes entangled in church affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got herself mixed up' rearranges the nine letters of COPPELIAS; Coppélia is a ballet whose title character is a doll.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal describes a church governed by bishops.

clue.text: Trainee broke a tool making a spindle

indicators.note: broke means the learner breaks into the tool word, splitting it

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
L, as on a learner driver's plate, stands for a trainee

explanation.surface: An apprentice damaged a tool while making a spindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' puts L inside AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Demanded a new desk

indicators.note: new indicates the word desk is made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone insisted on getting a fresh desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DESK into SKED, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for something firmly is to request or require it.

clue.text: Shows the light to many a politician

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so it stands for many
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Many a politician is shown the way.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb, lamp is an old or dialect word for illuminating something.
explanation.definitionFit: To lamp is to shine on or illuminate, an archaic verb sense.

clue.text: Pursuit of a horse

explanation.surface: A pastime connected with a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime pursued for pleasure, and a hobby was also an old name for a small horse.

clue.text: A young lady found to be at fault

parts.note: Miss is the title of a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl is judged to have done wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is wrong or faulty.

clue.text: Noisy bird after a vegetable or other bird

indicators.note: after means the second bird comes behind the vegetable

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
fowl is a general word for a bird

explanation.surface: A loud bird follows a vegetable or a second kind of bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacocks and peahens make loud, piercing cries.

clue.text: One is taken in by happy expressions which all mean the same thing

definitions.text: which all mean the same thing

indicators.note: is taken in by means the numeral goes inside the word for happy faces

parts.note: smiles are happy facial expressions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single person is fooled by cheerful faces that all say the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken in by' puts I inside SMILES.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter treats figures of speech comparing like with like as saying one thing is the same as another.

clue.text: Live in a normal way

parts.note: taken as written
a habit is someone's usual way of doing things

explanation.surface: Advice to live in an ordinary fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to dwell or reside there.

clue.text: Piece of music performed by Tom wearing an untidy coat

indicators.note: wearing means the cat is clothed by the jumbled coat letters
untidy means the letters of coat are disarranged

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A man named Tom in a scruffy coat plays a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges COAT to TOCA, and 'wearing' puts CAT inside it; Tom misleads as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a keyboard composition showing off rapid finger work.

clue.text: Argentine port dispatches Spanish lady to Brazilian port

parts.note: Rosa is a Spanish woman's name
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A harbour in Argentina sends a woman off to Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosario is a major river port on the Paraná in Argentina.

clue.text: Turned to trade perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of to trade might be put another way

explanation.surface: A merchant switched to commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TO TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotated has spun round on an axis.

clue.text: The meat's about right but it doesn't do any good

indicators.note: about means the word for meat is wrapped round the abbreviation for right

parts.note: ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: A diner says the meat is nearly fine but not nourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage or injury is the opposite of any benefit.

clue.text: A rather pretty accent

parts.note: cute means attractive in a sweet, rather pretty way

explanation.surface: A charming way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a regional voice; the definition is the written accent mark over a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute is a diacritic mark slanting upwards, as on the e in café.

clue.text: Girl who is found in Los Angeles

indicators.note: found in means the little word sits inside the city abbreviation

explanation.surface: A young woman discovered in California's largest city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts IS inside LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisa is a female first name.

clue.text: At the beginning of last month it turned cold

indicators.note: at the beginning takes the opening letter of it and places it at the front
turned means the abbreviation for the last month is read backwards

parts.note: Dec, December, is the last month of the year

explanation.surface: Early in December the weather became chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the beginning' gives I from 'it'; 'turned' reverses DEC to CED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chilled with frozen water has been made very cold.

clue.text: Foreign currency goes up and down

indicators.note: goes up and down says the word reads identically upwards and downwards in the grid

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An overseas currency fluctuates.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, reading the same both ways means it goes up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former coin of India, worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Put off in order to ascertain starting prices

indicators.note: in order suggests the jumbled letters must be sorted out

parts.note: the start of the word prices is its first two letters, P and R

explanation.surface: A bookmaker delays so as to check the starting prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges TO ASCERTAIN with PR, the start of 'prices'.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay or postpone doing something until later.

clue.text: Editor sees drawback of Scot taking an age following Victoria

parts.note: split as draw back: the word draw read backwards
Ian is a typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: An editor notes the drawback of a Scotsman who takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' splits into DRAW plus 'back', telling us to reverse DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edwardian era, 1901 to 1910, came after Queen Victoria's reign.
